info.name: E-tiGo API v1
info.description:
# E-tiGo API v1

**Ride-hailing platform API for Lagos, Abuja, and other Nigerian cities.**

## Quick Start

### 1. Environment Setup
Select **E-tiGo — Local** or **E-tiGo — Staging** from the Postman environment dropdown.

### 2. Seeded Test Accounts

All seeded accounts use the password: `Qwer!234`

#### Admin Accounts
| Email | Role | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `admin@etigo.com` | Super Admin | Default super admin account |
| `ops@etigo.com` | Operations | Operations manager |
| `safety@etigo.com` | Safety Operator | SOS/safety console access |
| `support@etigo.com` | Support | Customer support agent |
| `finance@etigo.com` | Finance | Finance & payments manager |

#### Passenger Accounts (OTP login)
| Phone | Email | Name |
|-------|-------|------|
| `+2348100000001` | `ade@demo.etigo.com` | Ade Ogunleye |
| `+2348100000002` | `ngozi@demo.etigo.com` | Ngozi Okafor |
| `+2348100000003` | `emeka@demo.etigo.com` | Emeka Nwosu |
| `+2348100000004` | `funmi@demo.etigo.com` | Funmi Adeyemi |
| `+2348100000005` | `chidi@demo.etigo.com` | Chidi Eze |

#### Driver Accounts (OTP login)
| Phone | Email | Name | Status | Vehicle |
|-------|-------|------|--------|---------|
| `+2348200000001` | `bayo@demo.etigo.com` | Bayo Akinola | Approved (Online) | Toyota Corolla (Economy, petrol) |
| `+2348200000002` | `kemi@demo.etigo.com` | Kemi Bakare | Approved (Offline) | Honda Accord (Comfort, hybrid) |
| `+2348200000003` | `segun@demo.etigo.com` | Segun Obaseki | Approved (Online) | Mercedes-Benz EQE (Premium, electric) |
| `+2348200000004` | `amara@demo.etigo.com` | Amara Nnamdi | Pending Review | Toyota Highlander (SUV, petrol) |
| `+2348200000005` | `tunde@demo.etigo.com` | Tunde Fashola | Suspended | Nissan Sentra (Economy, CNG) |
| `+2348200000006` | `ify@demo.etigo.com` | Ify Okoro | Rejected | — |

### 3. Seeded Data

#### Cities
| City | Status | Currency | Radius |
|------|--------|----------|--------|
| Lagos | Active | NGN | 40 km |
| Abuja | Active | NGN | 30 km |
| Port Harcourt | Active | NGN | 20 km |
| Ibadan | Inactive | NGN | 20 km |

#### Vehicle Classes
| Class | Display Name | Capacity |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| economy | Economy | 4 |
| comfort | Comfort | 4 |
| premium | Premium | 4 |
| suv | SUV | 6 |

#### Promo Codes
| Code | Type | Value | Status |
|------|------|-------|--------|
| `WELCOME50` | 50% off (max ₦2,000) | Active | 1 use per user |
| `RIDE500` | ₦500 flat discount | Active | 3 uses per user |
| `OFFPEAK20` | 20% off (off-peak only) | Active | 5 uses per user |
| `EXPIRED10` | 10% off | Expired | — |

### 4. Authentication Flow

**Passengers & Drivers:** Send OTP → Verify OTP → (if new user) Complete Registration → Use bearer token.

**Admins:** POST `/admin/auth/login` with email & password → Use bearer token.

All protected endpoints require: `Authorization: Bearer {token}`

### Static OTP (Non-Production Only)

In **local** and **staging** environments, all OTP codes are **`123456`**. Message delivery is skipped entirely. This lets you create and verify accounts freely without OTP costs.

1. `POST /auth/otp/send` with any valid phone → returns success immediately
2. `POST /auth/otp/verify` with same phone + code `123456` → logs in or prompts registration

**Production always generates random codes and delivers via WhatsApp (with SMS fallback).**

### 5. Rate Limiting
Auth routes (`/auth/*`, `/admin/auth/*`) are rate-limited to **5 requests/minute** per IP. Exceeding returns `429 Too Many Requests`.



### 6. Admin Roles & Permissions

E-tiGo uses role-based access control (RBAC) for admin endpoints. Super Admins bypass all role checks.

| Role | Value | Access |
|------|-------|--------|
| Super Admin | `super_admin` | Full system access, admin management |
| Operations | `operations` | Drivers, cities, vehicle classes, pricing, surge, rides, monitoring, fleet, gamification, promos, EV stations, offline flags, operational reports |
| Safety Operator | `safety_operator` | SOS console, drivers, passengers, offline flags |
| Support | `support` | Passengers, disputes, wallets (read-only), driver ledgers (read-only) |
| Finance | `finance` | Pricing, fleet, promos, wallets, ledger, adjustments, payouts, refunds, settings, all reports |

| Endpoint Group | Operations | Safety | Support | Finance |
|----------------|:----------:|:------:|:-------:|:-------:|
| Drivers (incl. vehicle class) | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| Cities / Vehicle Classes / Surge | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Pricing | ✅ | — | — | ✅ |
| Rides (pending, assign) / Live Monitoring | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Rides (refund) | — | — | — | ✅ |
| Fleet Vehicles / Fleet Agreements | ✅ | — | — | ✅ |
| Gamification | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Promos | ✅ | — | — | ✅ |
| EV Stations | ✅ | — | — | — |
| Offline Trip Flags | ✅ | ✅ | — | — |
| SOS Console | — | ✅ | — | — |
| Passengers | — | ✅ | ✅ | — |
| Disputes | — | — | ✅ | — |
| Wallets (view) / Driver Ledgers | — | — | ✅ | ✅ |
| Wallets (freeze), Ledger, Adjustments, Payouts, Settings | — | — | — | ✅ |
| Reports (financial / reconciliation) | — | — | — | ✅ |
| Reports (operational) | ✅ | — | — | ✅ |
| Admin Management | — | — | — | — |

### 7. Variables & Request Chaining

Select an environment first. Login and registration requests store `passenger_token`, `driver_token` or `admin_token` automatically (in the active environment and the collection).

**Run these once before anything else** — they store the seeded ids the other requests use:

1. **Public → List Active Cities** → `city_id` (Lagos)
2. **Public → List City Vehicle Classes** → `economy_class_id`, `comfort_class_id`, `premium_class_id`, `vehicle_class_id`

Other requests store ids as you go: **Create Ride** → `ride_id`, `share_token` · **Top Up Wallet** → `topup_reference` · **Initialize Payment** → `payment_reference` · **List All Drivers** → `driver_id`, `driver_user_id` · **Available Drivers for Ride** → `driver_user_id` · **Get Driver** → `document_id` · **List Wallets** → `account_id` · **Request Payout** → `payout_id` · **Create Adjustment** → `adjustment_id` · **Trigger SOS** → `sos_incident_id` · **Reserve EV Stall** → `ev_reservation_id` · **List Fleet Agreements** → `fleet_agreement_id` · **Get Fleet Agreement** → `remittance_id` · **Ledger Transactions** → `ledger_entry_id`. The admin *Create* requests (city, vehicle class, pricing, surge rule…) overwrite the matching id with the new record — re-run the two list requests above to switch back to the seeded data.

Every variable is declared on the collection, so nothing resolves to an undefined `{{...}}`. All ids are UUIDs.

### 8. Sessions

Admin dashboard tokens expire after `SANCTUM_TOKEN_EXPIRATION` minutes (default 480 = 8 h). Passenger and driver app tokens expire after `SANCTUM_APP_TOKEN_EXPIRATION` minutes (default 43,200 = 30 days). An expired token returns `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`.

---

## What Changed for the Apps (October 2026)
See `doc/technical/FRONTEND_UPDATE_PAYMENTS_EV_SURGE.md` for the payouts, tips, EV, fuel type and surge changes per app, breaking ones first.

## Content Type
- JSON: `Content-Type: application/json`
- File uploads: `Content-Type: multipart/form-data`

## Error Format
All errors return `{ "message": "...", "error_code": "..." }`. Validation errors (422) include an `errors` object with field-level details.

| Status | `error_code` | When |
|--------|--------------|------|
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | Missing, invalid or expired token |
| 403 | `HTTP_ERROR` | Wrong user type or admin role |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | `Resource not found.` (bad id) or `The requested endpoint does not exist.` (bad URL) |
| 409 | `INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` | The ride/SOS changed state concurrently (body includes `current_status`) |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Field validation failed (`errors` object) |
| 422 | `INVALID_PARAMETER` | A malformed id or date reached the database |
| 429 | `HTTP_ERROR` | Rate limited — honour the `Retry-After` header |
| 500 | `SERVER_ERROR` | Unexpected error (details only when debugging is enabled) |

request.description:
No auth required. Detects the active city for given coordinates.

**Detection flow:**
1. Reverse-geocode coordinates via Mapbox to get city name
2. Match name against active cities in database
3. If no name match, fall back to boundary matching:
   - Point: haversine distance <= radius_km
   - Polygon: ray-casting point-in-polygon algorithm
4. If multiple boundaries match (overlap), returns the smallest (most specific) city

**Overlap resolution:** when a coordinate falls inside multiple boundaries, the city with the smallest area wins. This lets you define a large metro-wide fallback zone with precise inner zones.

**Both boundary types supported:** Point+radius and Polygon can coexist in the same deployment.

Returns 404 if no active city matches.

request.description:
Returns the OAuth redirect URL for the given provider. The mobile app opens this URL in a system browser (not a WebView). After the user authorizes, the backend redirects to the app deep link: `etigo-{type}:///auth/callback?code=...&state=...`.

The app then calls `POST /auth/social/exchange` with the received `code` to get the session token.

**Parameters:**
- `provider` — One of: `google`, `apple`, `facebook`
- `type` — Must be `passenger` or `driver`. Determines the deep link scheme for the callback.
- `state` — A random CSRF-protection string (min 16 characters) that the app generates and verifies on callback.

No auth required. Rate-limited to 5 requests/minute.

response.name: 200 — Redirect URL
422 — Invalid Provider

request.description:
Exchange a one-time authorization code (received via deep link callback after social OAuth) for a session token. The code is single-use and expires after 5 minutes.

**Deep Link Flow:**
1. App calls `POST /auth/social/redirect` with `provider`, `type`, and a random `state`
2. App opens the returned `redirect_url` in a browser
3. User completes OAuth with the provider
4. Backend redirects to the app deep link: `etigo-{type}:///auth/callback?code=...&state=...`
5. App calls this endpoint with the `code` to get the session token

request.description:
Passenger token. Returns a quote for every active vehicle class in `{{city_id}}` (run **Public → List Active Cities** first).

- Distance and duration come from the maps provider (Google, then Mapbox, then a straight-line estimate).
- `fare_estimate` already includes the current surge and the passenger's loyalty-tier discount; the discount is also returned as `booking_fee_discount` (NGN).
- Booking (`POST /rides`) and the final fare use the same calculation. The quote is an upfront fare: it changes only for a waiting charge or a trip that runs significantly longer than the quoted time.
- Cross-city or very long trips return a `warnings` array. Inactive cities and identical pickup/destination return 422.

request.description:
Passenger books a ride. Uses `{{city_id}}` and `{{economy_class_id}}` (run **Public → List Active Cities** and **List City Vehicle Classes** first). **Sets `{{ride_id}}` and `{{share_token}}`.**

- Returns the ride (`reference_number` e.g. `TRP-NG-000123`) and the 4-digit `pin_code` for the driver.
- One active ride per passenger: a second booking returns 409.
- `payment_method`: `cash`, `card` (saved default card), `wallet` (a hold for the estimate is placed now) or `bank_transfer`.
- The surge multiplier and tier discount in effect now are locked in for the final fare.
- Optional `promo_code`: validated now against city, class, fare, time window, tier and usage limits — an invalid code rejects the booking with 422; the discount is applied at completion.
- To book for later, add `scheduled_pickup_at` — see **Book Scheduled Ride**. Ride responses carry `is_scheduled`, `scheduled_pickup_at` and `scheduled` (null for rides booked for now).

request.description:
Books a ride for later: `POST /rides` plus `scheduled_pickup_at` (ISO 8601 **with a UTC offset**). **Sets `{{scheduled_ride_id}}`.** Change the time in the body to one 30 minutes to 7 days from now before sending.

- The ride is created in `scheduled` status: no PIN (`pin_code` is `null`), no wallet hold, no matching yet. Matching starts `scheduled.dispatch_at` (15 min before pickup); the PIN appears on the ride then.
- The fare is quoted and locked now, with the surge in effect **at the pickup time** (time-based/manual rules; never demand surge). A promo code must be valid at the pickup time.
- Wallet bookings: the balance must cover the quote now; it is held at dispatch.
- Limits (operations-editable, see `GET /config` → `scheduled_rides`): 30 min to 7 days ahead, 5 upcoming bookings, 30 min apart.
- Booking for later works while the passenger is on another ride.

request.description:
Passenger tips once per completed ride (between the tip settings' min and max). `source` says how the tip is paid: `wallet`, `card` or `cash`, defaulting to the ride's payment method; the response's `payment.tip_method` records it.

- Card: charged to the default saved card first. A decline records nothing (422 "Failed to charge tip amount.") and the passenger can retry. If the bank does not answer, the tip stays reserved and is checked by its reference before anything is charged again (422 "We could not confirm your tip payment with the bank yet. Please try again in a few minutes; you will not be charged twice."); a later attempt settles it first ("Your earlier tip went through, so you were not charged again."). Credited to the driver in full.
- Wallet: paid from the passenger's wallet balance and credited to the driver in full. Balance too low → 422 "Your wallet balance is too low for this tip."; frozen or closed wallet → 422 "Wallet is frozen or closed."
- Cash: recorded only; the driver collects it in person. Only on cash rides (422 "Cash tips can only be recorded on cash rides.").
- Bank-transfer rides must send `source` (`wallet` or `card`): 422 "Choose how to pay the tip: wallet or card." otherwise.

A second tip → 422.

Returns a detailed receipt for a completed ride including fare breakdown, vehicle details, card info, tip, tier discount, promo discount, carbon emissions, and payment details. Accessible by the ride's passenger, driver, or any admin.

**`payment` totals** — exactly one is present:
- `total_charged` (number) — when `status` is `captured`, `collected` or `settled`; fare + tip actually charged.
- `amount_due` (string) — any other status (e.g. `pending`, `pending_collection` for cash not yet collected, `failed`); the fare still owed, without the tip.

`payment` is `null` when the ride has no payment record.

**`trip_time`** — fares are upfront. `duration_minutes` is the time billed; `trip_time` shows `quoted_minutes`, `actual_minutes` (trip start to completion, may be `null`), `billed_minutes` and `adjusted`. The quoted time is billed unless the trip ran more than 25% (and at least 10 minutes) longer; then the actual time is billed, capped at 3× the quote, and `adjusted` is `true` — show the passenger a note. `null` for rides completed before upfront fares.

**Errors:** 403 — not the ride's passenger or driver, and not an admin. 404 — the ride is not completed.

item.name: 🔐 Driver — KYC Verification
item.description:
KYC identity verification endpoints for drivers. Uses QoreID for NIN, Driver's License, Vehicle Plate, and Liveness verification.

**Required verifications for `verified` status:** NIN + Driver's License + Vehicle Plate.

**Test values (FakeKycGateway):**
- IDs starting with `000` → fail
- All other IDs → pass
- Liveness sessions with `fail` in session ID → fail

request.description:
**Auth required (driver).**

Returns the driver's aggregate KYC status and per-type verification summary.

**Response:** `200` with `{kyc_status, kyc_verified_at, verifications}`

**KYC Status values:** `not_started`, `in_progress`, `verified`, `failed`

401 — Unauthenticated

request.description:
**Auth required (driver).**

Submits a NIN for verification against QoreID. Name matching is performed against the driver's registered name.

**Required fields:**
- `nin_number` — string, exactly 11 digits

**Responses:**
- `200` — NIN verified successfully
- `422` — Verification failed (name mismatch, invalid NIN)
- `409` — Already verified or in progress

**Test:** Use `00012345678` to trigger a failure.

422 — Verification Failed

- `timestamp` (optional): a date/time; accepted but not used — the server's time is recorded

**Rate Limit:** 429 if called more than once per second.

item.name: Ride Actions
item.description: Driver-side ride lifecycle actions: accepting/rejecting dispatched ride requests, arriving at pickup, verifying passenger PIN, and completing rides.

request.description:
Driver accepts the ride they were offered (the matching engine offers one ride to one driver at a time; an unanswered offer expires after 20 s). The ride moves `searching` → `matched` → `driver_en_route`. The ride and the driver are locked, so the first acceptance wins and a driver can never hold two rides.

- 403 — the ride was not offered to this driver, or the driver's earnings balance is below the allowed negative threshold.
- 409 — another driver already accepted, or the driver already has an active ride.
- 422 — the ride is no longer open for acceptance.

Driver reserves a charging stall. **Electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles only**: the vehicle's `fuel_type` must be `electric` or `plug_in_hybrid` (`can_charge: true` on the vehicle), otherwise 422. Three outcomes:

1. **reserved** (201) — a stall was free and is locked for 30 minutes (`EV_RESERVATION_EXPIRY`); not activated by then, it expires and goes to the next driver in the queue.
2. **queued** (200) — all stalls busy but one frees up within 15 minutes; the driver is notified when it is theirs.
3. **retry** (200) — no stall soon; try again after `retry_after_minutes`.

**Reservation fee** (₦500, `EV_RESERVATION_FEE`; waived for Platinum and Diamond drivers, `fee_waived: true`). It is taken from the driver's available earnings when a stall is actually held for them: at once for `reserved`, on promotion for `queued`. `fee_charged_at` shows when. Like cash-ride commission, it may take the balance below zero down to the wallet's `max_negative_balance`; beyond that → 422 "Your earnings balance cannot cover the ₦500.00 reservation fee." (also checked before queueing). A driver whose earnings account is frozen → 422 "Your earnings account is on hold, so the reservation fee cannot be paid. Contact support." A queued driver who can no longer pay when a stall frees up is cancelled (reason in `notes`), gets an `ev_reservation_cancelled` push, and the stall goes to the next driver. Refunded on cancellation within 2 minutes of being charged (`EV_RESERVATION_FREE_CANCEL_MINUTES`); kept after that and on a no-show. `free_cancellation_until` gives the deadline for a countdown (null when there is nothing to refund).

One open reservation per driver (422). **Sets `{{ev_reservation_id}}`.**

response.name: 404 — No Account

request.description:
Resolves the account with Paystack and saves it as the driver's primary payout account.

Every save needs `otp_code`, the first account included: call **Request Bank Account Code** first (non-production code: `123456`). Without it → 422 `errors.otp_code`; a wrong or expired code → 422 `errors.otp_code` with the reason.

Paystack resolves the account before the code is checked, so a resolve failure does not use up the code. Each save notifies the driver (`payout_account_changed`, in-app and push) and sends a WhatsApp/SMS alert regardless of preferences.

Payout safeguards: the response has `payout_eligibility` (`can_request_payouts`, `code`, `message`, `payouts_held_until`). A replacement account is held for the `payout_account_hold_hours` wallet setting (default 24); a name mismatch is saved for finance review (default) or refused in `block` mode (422 `code: payout_account_name_mismatch`, code not used up). **Sets `{{payout_account_id}}`.**

response.name: 200 — Payouts

request.description:
Driver requests a withdrawal (kobo, at least the `min_payout` wallet setting, default 100000 = ₦1,000) to their verified bank account. **Sets `{{payout_id}}`.**

Lifecycle: `requested` → `approved` (finance) → `processing` (transfer sent) → `paid`, or `rejected` / `failed` / `reversed`. The money leaves the available balance when the transfer is sent; a failed or reversed transfer returns it. If Paystack cannot be reached, answers with a server error or never confirms, the payout stays `approved` or `processing` with the money reserved until Paystack's answer is known (checked automatically every 15 minutes); it is never lost or paid twice. One open payout at a time (422), rate limit 3/min. Blocked by a payout safeguard on the bank account → 422 with `code` (`payout_account_on_hold`, `payout_account_under_review`, `payout_account_rejected`) and `payouts_held_until`.

request.description:
Creates a new city/service area.

**Required fields:** name, state
**Optional fields:** boundary, vehicle_class_ids, timezone, currency_code

**Auto-derived by backend:**
- region — derived from state (e.g. Lagos → South-West)
- slug — generated from name, auto-suffixed if duplicate
- area_sq_km — calculated from Polygon boundary coordinates
- is_active — defaults to true
- timezone — defaults to Africa/Lagos if not sent
- currency_code — defaults to NGN if not sent

**Boundary types:**
- Point + radius_km: circular service area (simpler setup)
- Polygon: custom shape with coordinates array (admin draws on map)

**State validation:** must be one of the 36 Nigerian states or FCT. Use GET /lookup/states to populate the dropdown.

**Vehicle classes:** pass an array of UUIDs from GET /admin/vehicle-classes. They are synced (replaces any existing associations).

item.name: Admin — Manual Assignment
item.description:
**Required Role(s):** Operations (Super Admin always has access)

Manual assignment of drivers to rides that automatic matching did not place (support escalations, `no_driver_found`).

### Flow
1. **List Pending Rides** — saves the first ride as `{{ride_id}}`.
2. **Available Drivers for Ride** — saves the nearest driver's user id as `{{driver_user_id}}`.
3. **Manually Assign Driver** — assigns `{{driver_user_id}}` to `{{ride_id}}`.

### Assignment is instant
There is no request for the driver to accept or decline. The ride goes straight to `matched` → `driver_en_route`, the driver and passenger are notified, and admins get `ride.status.updated`. So there is no answer timeout and nothing to cancel while waiting; to undo an assignment the ride is cancelled as usual.

### How "available" is decided
Online and approved · reported GPS in the last 2 minutes · not on a trip (`matched`, `driver_en_route`, `driver_arrived`, `in_progress`) · in the ride's city · vehicle in the ride's class · within `radius_km` (default 5 km) of the pickup · nearest first.

### Keeping the list current (WebSocket)
Private channel `admin.rides`, event `ride.status.updated` (`ride_id, passenger_id, driver_id, previous_status, status, actor_type, actor_id, occurred_at`):
- **new pending ride** → `status` = `searching` (from `requested`)
- **no driver found** → `status` = `no_driver_found`
- **ride matched** → `status` = `matched` / `driver_en_route` (`actor_type` = `admin` for a manual assignment)
- **ride cancelled** → `status` = `cancelled`

See **Real-Time (WebSocket) → Authorize Channel — Admin** for subscribing.

### Common errors
`401 UNAUTHENTICATED` · `403` insufficient admin role · `404 NOT_FOUND` unknown ride · `422 INVALID_PARAMETER` a malformed UUID filter.

### Test data on staging
`php artisan db:seed --class=MonitoringDemoSeeder` seeds 3 pending rides in Lagos (2 `searching`, 1 `no_driver_found`) with online demo drivers 0.8–6.5 km from their pickups, plus active rides at every stage. Demo drivers report their location every minute via the scheduler, each has rated past trips, and they are never offered rides by automatic matching (manual assignment only). Re-run the seeder to reset rides used up by testing.

query.description: Comma-separated: requested, searching, no_driver_found, matched, driver_en_route. Omit for unassigned rides only. Admin-assigned rides are driver_en_route, so include it for a "Matched" tab.
Partial, case-insensitive: trip reference, passenger name, city name or vehicle class name

request.description:
Rides waiting for a driver — `requested`, `searching` or `no_driver_found` with no driver — **oldest first**. `no_driver_found` rides drop off 24 hours after they were requested. Pass `status` to include matched rides (`matched`, `driver_en_route`).

**Matched rows** also carry `driver` (name, phone), `driver_rating`, `driver_vehicle` (`make`, `model`, `colour`, `plate_number`) and `matched_at` (when the driver accepted or the admin assigned).

**`summary`** (follows `city_id` and the 24-hour window only):
- `awaiting_driver` — unassigned `requested` + `searching` + `no_driver_found`. Use it for the **"needs attention" badge** on the Rides tab.
- `by_status` — counts for each status the list can show.

Saves the first ride's id as `{{ride_id}}`.

request.description:
Drivers who can take `{{ride_id}}`, **nearest first**.

Eligible = online and approved, GPS reported in the last 2 minutes, not on a trip, in the ride's city, vehicle in the ride's class, within `radius_km` of the pickup.

Per driver: `name`, `phone`, `rating` (null when unrated), `vehicle` (`make`, `model`, `plate_number`, `colour`, `vehicle_class`), `location` (with `updated_at`), `distance_km` (straight line to pickup) and `eta_minutes` (that distance at 30 km/h).

Saves the nearest driver's **user id** as `{{driver_user_id}}` — the id **Manually Assign Driver** expects.

request.description:
Assigns `{{driver_user_id}}` (a driver's **user** id — `user_id` from Available Drivers) to `{{ride_id}}`. **Instant**: the ride goes straight to `driver_en_route`; there is no accept/decline step.

The ride must be `requested`, `searching` or `no_driver_found`. For `no_driver_found`, it is refused if the passenger has booked again since, and a wallet ride's fare hold is placed again.

**Errors**
| Status | `error_code` | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | `errors.driver_id`: required / not a UUID / unknown user, `No driver profile found for this user.`, `Driver must be approved.`, `Driver must be online.`, `Driver vehicle class does not match the ride request.`, `Driver already has an active ride.` |
| 422 | `RIDE_NOT_ASSIGNABLE` | Ride is no longer `requested`/`searching`/`no_driver_found` (`current_status` says what it is) |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | `errors.ride`: `The passenger already has another active ride.` or a wallet hold error (`no_driver_found` rides) |
| 409 | `INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION` | The ride changed state while being assigned (e.g. a driver accepted it) — refresh and retry |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Unknown ride |
| 403 | — | Admin is not Operations / Super Admin |

item.name: Admin — Live Monitoring

query.description: Filter by ride status (e.g. matched, driver_en_route, driver_arrived, in_progress)

request.description:
Rides in an active status with the driver's live position. Use it to fill the map on load.

Per ride:
- `driver_location` — `lat`, `lng`, `heading`, `speed`, `timestamp`, `updated_at` (ISO 8601); `null` if the driver app hasn't reported for 5 minutes.
- `driver_rating`.
- `eta` — `target` = `pickup` while `matched`/`driver_en_route` (minutes for the driver to reach the passenger), `destination` while `in_progress`; `null` otherwise. From the driver's last routed ETA, else a straight-line estimate.
- `stage_timestamps` — `requested_at`, `matched_at`, `driver_en_route_at` (driver set off), `driver_arrived_at`, `started_at`.
- `has_active_sos` and `sos` — `trigger_type` and `raised_by.role` are who raised it (`passenger` / `driver`); `raised_by` adds `user_id` and `name`.

Saves a ride (the one with an open SOS, if any) as `{{monitoring_ride_id}}` for **Get Ride Detail**.

request.description:
One ride for the ride details panel — same fields as a **List Active Rides** row, any status — plus:

- `driver_vehicle` — `make`, `model`, `colour`, `plate_number`, `vehicle_class`.
- `route` — planned pickup → destination route: `encoded_polyline` (Google encoded polyline, precision 5; decode with `google.maps.geometry.encoding.decodePath` or `@mapbox/polyline`), `distance_km`, `duration_minutes`. Cached per ride. `null` if the routing provider is down — fall back to a straight line.

Run **List Active Rides** first to set `{{monitoring_ride_id}}`.

request.description:
Resolve or dismiss a dispute. Optionally issue a card refund when resolving. Creates an audit log entry.

**Request fields:**
- `status`: `resolved` or `dismissed`
- `resolution_notes`: required, 10–2000 characters
- `refund_amount`: optional, numeric, min 1. Only valid with status `resolved` and card payments.

**Refund rules:**
- Cannot refund on dismissal
- Cannot refund cash payments
- Cannot exceed the ride's payment amount
- Supports partial refunds

**Validation:**
- Cannot resolve/dismiss a dispute already in a terminal state

request.description:
Paginated payout requests. Filters: `status`, `search` (driver name/email), `from`/`to` (date range).

`needs_attention` is `true` when the transfer outcome has been unconfirmed for longer than usual: approved for over 10 minutes without being sent, or processing for over 30 minutes without Paystack's confirmation. Show a **Check status** button for those payouts that calls *Check Payout Status (Paystack)*.

`attention_reason` explains the flag: `awaiting_otp` (Paystack is holding the transfer for an OTP; turn off transfer OTP in the Paystack dashboard, then check status; flagged immediately), `not_sent` or `unconfirmed`. `provider_status` is Paystack's last reported status for the transfer. Each payout has `bank_account_block` (`null` or `code`, `message`, `payouts_held_until`): disable Approve/Retry when set.

request.description:
Finance retries a `failed` or `reversed` payout; in both cases the money is back in the driver's balance. The job first checks the previous transfer with Paystack: if it actually went through, the payout is marked paid instead of sending again. Otherwise the money is sent again under a new transfer reference (`PAYOUT-{id}-2`, `-3`, …), as Paystack advises after a definite failure. Any other status → 422.

For a payout stuck in `approved` or `processing`, use *Check Payout Status (Paystack)* instead. Refused with 409 while the payout's bank account is on hold, under review or rejected (`code`): resolve it under **Payout Accounts** first.

response.name: 200 — Retrying
422 — Not Failed or Reversed
409 — Bank Account Under Review

request.description:
Finance's **Check status** action for a payout whose transfer outcome is unknown — show it when the payout has `needs_attention: true` (approved for over 10 minutes without being sent, e.g. Paystack was unreachable for every attempt, or processing for over 30 minutes without Paystack's confirmation). It asks Paystack about the payout's transfer reference and settles the payout. The driver's money stays reserved until the outcome is known, and a transfer Paystack already has is never sent twice.

| `outcome` | Meaning | Payout afterwards |
|---|---|---|
| `paid` | Paystack completed the transfer | `paid` |
| `failed` | Paystack failed or reversed it; the money is back in the driver's balance | `reversed` — use *Retry Failed Payout* |
| `processing` | Paystack is still working on it | `processing` |
| `resent` | Paystack never received it; sent again under the same reference | `approved`, then `processing` |
| `unknown` | Processing, but Paystack has no transfer with this reference — contact Paystack support | unchanged |

`provider_status` is Paystack's own status (`success`, `failed`, `reversed`, `pending`, …). The scheduler runs the same check every 15 minutes, so most payouts settle without anyone pressing the button. Paystack unreachable → 502 (nothing changed; try again). Not `approved` or `processing` → 422 with `current_status`. Audited as `payout.verified`. Role: finance.

request.description:
A ride participant raises an SOS on an active ride. Simultaneous taps open a single incident.

1. A WhatsApp alert (SMS fallback) with GPS and trip details is queued to the E-tiGo safety desk — independent of the WebSocket server.
2. After 5 s the user gets an "Are you safe?" check-in; no answer within 30 s escalates the incident to the console (`sos.incident.escalated`).
3. `sos.incident.triggered` is broadcast on `admin.sos`.

The response includes `auto_dial_emergency: "112"` — the app should start that call. **Sets `{{sos_incident_id}}`.** 409 if an open incident exists for the ride; 422 if the ride is not active or the user is not a participant.

request.description:
Authorize a private WebSocket channel subscription. Called automatically by the Pusher/Echo client library during channel subscription.

**Channels:**
- `private-ride.{rideId}` — Authorized for the ride's passenger or assigned driver
- `private-admin.rides` — Authorized for admin users only

**Events received on these channels:**
- `driver.location.updated` — Real-time driver GPS (lat, lng, heading, speed, timestamp, ride_id, eta)

**WebSocket Connection:**
Connect to the Reverb WebSocket server using Laravel Echo or a Pusher-compatible client:
- Host: `REVERB_HOST` (default: localhost)
- Port: `REVERB_PORT` (default: 8080)
- App Key: `REVERB_APP_KEY`
- Auth endpoint: `POST /broadcasting/auth` with Bearer token

response.name: 200 — Authorized
403 — Unauthorized

request.description:
Authorize subscription to the admin rides channel. Receives all `driver.location.updated` events across all active rides for the admin dashboard.

### `admin.rides` events
- `driver.location.updated` — `driver_id, lat, lng, heading, speed, timestamp, ride_id, eta` (driver positions for the live map).
- `ride.status.updated` — `ride_id, passenger_id, driver_id, previous_status, status, actor_type, actor_id, occurred_at`. For the pending list: new pending ride = `searching`; no driver found = `no_driver_found`; matched = `matched`/`driver_en_route`; cancelled = `cancelled`.

With Laravel Echo: `Echo.private('admin.rides').listen('.ride.status.updated', handler)` (note the leading dot).

item.name: Webhooks

request.description:
**Single Paystack webhook URL.** No auth — verified by HMAC-SHA512 (`x-paystack-signature`) with `PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY`.

- `charge.success` with a `TOPUP-` reference → wallet top-up (credited once).
- `charge.success` (other) → ride payment: re-verified with Paystack by reference, amount and currency checked, then captured and settled.
- `transfer.success` → payout paid; `transfer.failed` / `transfer.reversed` → payout failed and the money returned to the driver.

Events are stored per provider + event id + event type. A fully processed redelivery returns "Already processed."; an event whose processing failed part-way is processed again when Paystack retries — every handler is idempotent.

response.name: 200 — Webhook Received
200 — Already Processed (duplicate)
403 — Invalid Signature

request.description:
**Paystack's transfer Approval URL** (Settings → Preferences → Transfer Approval). Called by Paystack before every transfer, not by the apps. No auth: the endpoint changes nothing and approves only what is already in our database.

- `200` approves the transfer, `400` rejects it. No answer within a few seconds blocks it.
- Approved only if `reference` is a payout's `gateway_reference` (`PAYOUT-{id}`, `PAYOUT-{id}-2`, …), the payout is `approved` or `processing`, `amount` (kobo) equals the payout amount, `currency` (if sent) is `NGN`, and `recipient` is the recipient code saved on the payout before the transfer started.
- Anything else, such as a transfer started with a leaked secret key or made by hand in the dashboard, is rejected and logged as critical. The reason is logged, not returned.
- Paystack doesn't document the exact shape, so every object with a `reference` is treated as a transfer: at the top level, under `data`, or in a list (bulk), up to three levels deep. All of them must match. `recipient` may be an object carrying `recipient_code`.
- A rejection logs the request's shape (keys and types, no values) for diagnosis.

To try it locally, send a transfer whose reference, amount and recipient match an approved payout (200). Change any one of them to get 400.

response.name: 200 — Transfer Approved
400 — Transfer Rejected

header.description: HMAC-SHA256 signature (optional in dev when QOREID_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set)

request.description:
**No auth required** — verified by HMAC-SHA256 signature.

Receives liveness verification results from QoreID.

**Handled events:** `verification_completed`, `step_verification_completed`, `identity`

**Headers:**
- `X-QoreID-Signature` — HMAC-SHA256 of body using `QOREID_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (optional in dev when secret is not configured)

**Responses:**
- `200` — Webhook processed
- `401` — Invalid signature
- `400` — Missing session ID

response.name: 200 — Webhook Processed
400 — Invalid Signature

request.description:
**Flutterwave failover webhook.** No auth — verified by the `verif-hash` header (`FLUTTERWAVE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`).

- `charge.completed` (status `successful`) with a `TOPUP-` tx_ref → wallet top-up (amounts in naira, converted to kobo).
- `charge.completed` (other) → ride payment verification.
- `transfer.completed` → paid only when `data.status` is `SUCCESSFUL`, otherwise failed; `transfer.failed` → failed.

Same deduplication as Paystack. Payouts currently go through Paystack only.
